item: Cylinder block, head, crank, pistons, cams and lash adjusters
why: The engine itself; opened further only if BD07 calls for it
then: Serviced per DR06

item: Timing belt, tensioner, idler, water pump, cam and crank seals
why: Wear parts; the seller's terms and good practice both require them at install
then: EN03 (DR06)

item: Front engine cover, timing covers, crank pulley
then: Cleaned; pulley checked for wobble

item: Cam angle sensor (CAS) on the intake cam's rear
why: It is the engine's trigger: the EMU Black reads it (SGT and SGC signals, S-623 tests with codes)
then: Its pin-out and pattern go to BP05
note: A 1996-97 BP adds a crank sensor at the crank pulley - which year is BP01

item: Engine harness pieces and their cut pigtails
why: The ECU and harness stay in the electrical project; the new leg is BP05
then: The pigtails are saved for their connector bodies

item: Alternator (Miata)
why: D-633: the FD RX-7 100 A on the BP's bracket
then: AC02
note: The Miata unit is kept as a spare or sold

item: Power-steering pump, its bracket and belt
why: Luxury's power steering (04-luxury C12, D-636)
then: Runs unloaded until luxury plumbs it, or comes off with the bracket kept if luxury picks electric

item: A/C compressor, its bracket and belt
why: Luxury's A/C (the engine keeps it mounted)
then: Its hoses, condenser and charge come with luxury; the clutch is unpowered until then

item: Starter
why: If on the engine (BP01) it is kept
then: Its cable and solenoid wire are the electrical project's

item: Engine mount brackets (the arms bolted to the block)
why: Their bolt holes and faces are what DS07's adapter plates bolt to
then: DS07

item: Engine hanger brackets
why: To lift the engine

item: Oil pan, pickup and drain plug
why: The stock wet sump suits a street FB; a turbo-return bung is welded in while it is off (OL02)
then: DS02 checks it against the FB crossmember

item: Oil-pressure switch or sender
why: The PMU's fuel-pump gate and the ICU want a real pressure signal (HO04)
then: A pressure sensor on a tee with a plugged turbo-feed port (OL01)

item: Oil cooler (coolant-to-oil, at the oil filter)
why: The 1994 BP has one (S-615 lubrication section, page 130); it steadies oil temperature, more so with a turbo
then: Its coolant hoses go in BP07's hose plan
note: Confirm it is on the engine in hand

item: Oil filter and dipstick tube
then: Filter access checked in DS02

item: Water pump, thermostat and housing, coolant outlets
why: The pump and thermostat are renewed (DR06)
then: BP07 plans the hoses; the rear-outlet reroute is an option

item: Coolant temperature sensor (ECU) and gauge sender
why: The ECU reads its own sensor; the ICU takes coolant temperature from the ECU on CAN (HO06)
then: The gauge sender is plugged or left unwired

item: Radiator fan thermo-switch
why: The ECU switches the fan (HO02)
then: The port is plugged

item: Vane airflow meter (with the intake air temperature sensor inside it)
why: The EMU Black runs speed-density on MAP; the meter restricts the intake
then: A separate IAT sensor in the intake tube (DR04) and a MAP signal

item: Air cleaner box, resonance chamber and intake hose
why: The FB's own cold-air path (DR04)
then: AI01

item: Throttle body
Throttle position sensor (manual-gearbox type: an idle switch only)
why: The M/T TP sensor has only idle contacts (S-623, TP sensor continuity M/T), and the EMU Black needs a linear signal
then: A linear TP sensor: the Miata automatic's or an NB one, with an adapter (DR04)
note: Confirm which one the engine has at BD01

item: Idle speed control valve
why: The EMU Black drives it (code 34, idle speed control, S-623)

item: Fast-idle air valve (coolant-heated)
why: Helps cold idle; the EMU Black's idle control can make it unnecessary
then: Kept until the tune shows it is not needed

item: Intake manifold and its supports
Throttle cable bracket on the intake
why: The FB pedal's cable is fitted to it (DR04)

item: Cruise control cable bracket
why: No cruise on the FB's engine

item: Fuel rail, injectors, pressure regulator
why: Return-style with the manifold-referenced regulator (D-630)
then: Injectors cleaned and flow-tested (RB05)

item: Pressure regulator control (PRC) solenoid
why: A hot-restart aid the EMU Black does not need
then: The regulator's vacuum line goes straight to the manifold

item: Exhaust manifold and heat shield
why: Kept if it clears the FB's steering box (DS03, CD06)

item: Upstream O2 sensor (heated)
why: Emissions (D-622's rule, kept by D-630); the wideband is separate
then: A 1996-97 engine also has a downstream one

item: EGR valve, EGR vacuum and vent solenoids, EGR function sensor
why: The 1994 tests list EGR codes (16, 28, 29, S-623) but the 1994 vacuum diagram shows no EGR, so it is likely a California or automatic fit
then: If fitted, kept and run by the ECU so the car passes as its year (BP02 asks)

item: Purge solenoid and its hoses (EVAP)
why: Emissions (D-630)
then: The canister is the FB's or a yard Miata's (J6)

item: PCV valve and breather hoses
why: Required crankcase ventilation
then: Re-routed to the new intake tube (DR04)

item: Coil pack, plug wires, spark plugs
why: The plugs are renewed (DR06)
then: Whether an igniter is needed with the EMU Black is BP05's

item: 5-speed gearbox
why: Serviced per BD06
then: TR01

item: Flywheel, clutch disc and pressure plate (inside the bellhousing)
why: A used clutch is renewed while it is apart; the flywheel is resurfaced
then: CL05, CL06
note: Present per the photos (the gearbox is bolted on) - confirm at BD06

item: Clutch slave cylinder and release fork
why: If on the gearbox (BP01) the slave is kept or renewed with the release bearing
then: BP10

item: Gear lever and its boot
why: In the photos
then: Its position against the FB tunnel is J4

item: Neutral and reverse switches and their pigtails
why: The crank interlock and reverse lamps (electrical Y81)

item: Speedometer drive
why: Road speed for the ICU (electrical Y82)
note: Which drive this year has is confirm

item: Power plant frame (PPF)
why: Not in the package; the Miata's PPF ties the gearbox to its own diff, which the FB does not have
then: A fabricated gearbox crossmember on the PPF bosses (DS07); a yard PPF only as a template (J6)
